summary:
**SPHEREx Sky Viewer** is an open-source interactive web platform that transforms NASA’s SPHEREx all-sky infrared survey into an accessible, dynamic cosmic cinema.

While SPHEREx scans the entire sky every six months across 102 infrared spectral channels, exploring this multi-epoch data traditionally requires navigating massive FITS archives, custom coordinate re-projections, and complex calibrations. We developed a browser-based application integrating an interactive 360° celestial sky map with an aligned blink and difference-imaging engine. Our automated pipeline standardizes brightness stretching, masks detector artifacts, and strictly isolates spectral detectors to eliminate false variability caused by the satellite's Linear Variable Filters (LVF). In seconds, users can visually track stellar proper motion (such as Barnard’s Star) and photometric variability (such as R Draconis) accompanied by publication-ready light curves.

This platform addresses the challenge by unlocking the serendipitous time-domain discoveries hidden inside a mission designed for cosmology. By removing technical and computational barriers, SPHEREx Sky Viewer democratizes NASA's open data—empowering students, educators, citizen scientists, and astronomers worldwide to explore our moving universe with a single click.
details:
SPHEREx Explorer (team MINIONS)

What it does: SPHEREx Explorer turns NASA SPHEREx infrared images into short time-lapse "videos" of the sky. Visitors pick a star or type any coordinates, and the site plays real SPHEREx images of that spot in date order on a 360° sky map, so they can see nearby stars move or change brightness. Before that, a 3D scene shows where SPHEREx orbits Earth.

Benefits: No astronomy tools, data files or code are needed: one click takes you from a star name to a time-lapse. The site is honest about its limits: demo and simulated data are clearly labelled.

Intended impact: Students, teachers and sky fans can see, with real NASA images, that stars really move. It makes NASA's newest all-sky survey easy to explore and understand.

Tools: React, TypeScript and Python (FastAPI). Aladin Lite draws the sky map and three.js the 3D scene. Astropy processes the images, and Supabase holds the database. The data comes from NASA/IPAC IRSA (SPHEREx), Gaia DR3 and SIMBAD. The site is hosted on Vercel.

Creativity: SPHEREx was built to map the sky in colour. We reuse its visits to the same spot about every six months to show change over time, playing the images on top of the whole sky. The visit is a journey: from Earth, to where the telescope is, to looking through its eyes.

Factors considered: Scientific accuracy, including rejecting saturated images. The real limits of the data: tiny motions and only a few dates per star. Ease of use for beginners, accessibility, mobile support, and keeping the site working when NASA servers are slow.
